report.title: Waiver wire and opening market -- 2026 week 2
report.covers: week 2's waiver window; settlements also span week 1 (Tue 2026-09-08 03:00 - Tue 2026-09-15 03:00 ET)

summary_markdown:
The decision due today is a single waiver claim, and the add-candidate block points at one name clearly enough that the rest of the window is housekeeping. Treat the `gap` column here as what it is: the projected points gained by adding the candidate *and* benching the weakest eligible player already on the roster, not the candidate's projection outright. Two of the listed adds shrink to almost nothing once that bench move is priced in.

Against last week's report, the notable change is on the market side rather than the wire. The opening spreads moved toward the same side the projections already favoured, so nothing in the slate argues against the lineup that was trending anyway, and no settlement from week 1 reopened a roster spot that was assumed closed.

What this report cannot see: it has no injury news later than the freshness stamps above, it does not know which claims the other eleven managers have already submitted, and every row marked `insufficient data` is a refusal to print a number, not a zero.
